records.title: Extracellular Vesicles for Space Biomedical Research.
records.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are regulated, information-rich nanovesicles that reflect aspects of parent-cell state, making them promising readouts on biological adaptation. Microgravity perturbs mechanotransduction, mitochondrial stress and quality control, and autophagy-endolysosomal trafficking, processes that can reshape EV biogenesis and cargo selection. However, spaceflight EV studies remain sparse and methodologically inconsistent, complicating mechanistic interpretation and cross-mission comparison. In this review, we define an EV-centred framework that links microgravity-sensitive changes in cytoskeletal tension, membrane trafficking, mitochondrial quality control, and autophagy-endolysosomal routing to four measurable EV outputs: concentration, subtype balance, surface phenotype, and molecular cargo. We use this framework to organize current evidence from spaceflight and simulated microgravity studies, while considering the limitations introduced by heterogeneous isolation and characterization methods. We then examine microgravity-relevant EV culture systems, including high-density three-dimensional tissues, organoids, spheroids, and perfused tissue chips that support serial collection of conditioned media or effluent, together with compact capture and concentration approaches and core characterization strategies. Finally, we discuss the potential use of EVs as longitudinal liquid-biopsy readouts of stress and aging-like trajectories, as regenerative products relevant to musculoskeletal, vascular, and immune risks, and as engineered delivery vehicles. We identify EV uptake and biodistribution under altered gravity as a major translational gap and emphasize the need for standardized workflows that improve experimental rigor and biological interpretation in spaceflight research.

records.title: Divergent susceptibility of peripheral and central neurons to macrophages with a neurotoxic phenotype.
records.abstract: Macrophages play pivotal roles in neural injury responses, yet their influence on neuronal degeneration or regeneration differs markedly between the peripheral and central nervous systems. We investigated transcriptional and functional phenotypes of macrophages stimulated with agents reported to promote axonal regeneration and compared their effects on peripheral and central neurons. Classical M1/M2 polarization markers failed to reliably predict the functional output of pharmacologically stimulated macrophages. Zymosan-treated macrophage-conditioned medium (MCM) robustly enhanced neurite outgrowth in dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons without neurotoxicity, despite upregulating both M1 and M2 marker genes. In contrast, MCMs under all stimulation conditions induced pronounced neurite degeneration in cortical neurons, characterized by axonal fragmentation and α-spectrin cleavage. Co-culturing macrophages with peripheral DRG neurons markedly attenuated this neurotoxic phenotype. This neuroprotective effect was recapitulated in human cortical organoids, a physiologically relevant 3D model of human brain tissue, in which peripheral neuron-macrophage co-culture conditioned medium preserved neurofilament integrity and suppressed axonal injury markers. Cytokine profiling identified CCL3 and CCL5 as key regulators: CCL3, upregulated by neuron-macrophage interaction, conferred neuroprotection, while CCL5 contributed to MCM-induced neurotoxicity. These findings directly demonstrate that macrophage neurotoxicity is dichotomous, with PNS neurons largely resistant to the degenerative effects of macrophage-derived factors, whereas CNS neurons undergo robust neurodegeneration that can be modulated by peripheral neuron-macrophage interactions that reshape macrophage-derived cytokine expression profiles.

records.title: RDP-modified extracellular vesicles from brain organoid-derived mesenchymal stem cells improve the behavior and pathology of 5×FAD mice.
records.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder for which treatment options remain limited. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) offer a potential cell-free therapeutic approach, but limited brain exposure after systemic administration remains a major obstacle. Mesenchymal stem-like cells derived from human brain organoids (hBO-MSCs) may provide an alternative EV source with a molecular profile shaped by the neural culture environment. This study aimed to generate RDP-modified hBO-MSC-EVs and evaluate their physicochemical characteristics, acute safety, brain-associated biodistribution, and treatment-associated effects in the 5×FAD mouse model of AD. hBO-MSCs were isolated from dorsal forebrain-like human brain organoids and engineered to express an RDP-Lamp2b-HA fusion protein. EV preparations were characterized by morphology, particle measurements, EV-associated protein markers, and relative RDP-Lamp2b-HA abundance. Brain-associated biodistribution and acute safety were assessed in C57BL/6J mice, whereas treatment-associated outcomes were evaluated in 5×FAD mice receiving PBS, unmodified hBO-MSC-EVs, or hBO-MSC-RDP-EVs. Behavioral testing, hippocampal Aβ histopathology, and exploratory transcriptomic profiling were used to assess the response. Following intravenous administration, RDP modification was associated with greater brain-associated fluorescence than unmodified EVs, without evidence of overt acute organ histopathology or a consistent systemic pro-inflammatory response at the tested endpoints. In 5×FAD mice, hBO-MSC-RDP-EV treatment was associated with improvements in selected behavioral measures, most consistently in the Morris water maze, together with reduced histologically detectable hippocampal Aβ plaque burden and changes in inflammation- and neuronal-associated transcripts. These findings warrant further preclinical evaluation of surface-engineered hBO-MSC-EVs as a candidate cell-free approach for AD. Intact-EV blood-brain barrier transport, cargo-dependent mechanisms, source-specific advantages, and long-term safety remain unestablished.

records.title: Future directions and challenges of drug development and non-human primate models.
records.abstract: Gene and cell therapy are transforming therapeutic approaches for genetic diseases and malignancies. This review examines the current role and future directions of non-human primate (NHP) models in preclinical safety evaluation of adeno-associated virus (AAV) gene therapy and chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy amid accelerating adoption of new approach methodologies (NAMs). We systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure for publications from January 2015 to June 2026; approximately 60 English-language and 5 Chinese-language publications, together with FDA, EMA, and NMPA guidance documents, were included. NHPs remain the reference species for AAV and CAR-T safety evaluation, yet supply crises, ethical pressures, and documented prediction gaps (hepatotoxicity, dorsal root ganglion injury) are driving NAMs adoption. Organoids, organs-on-chips (87% sensitivity and 100% specificity for drug-induced liver injury), and AI-driven models are maturing under the FDA Modernization Act 2.0 and the 2025 FDA roadmap. We propose the Hierarchical Replacement Assessment Framework (HRAF), a three-tier, two-threshold model that reallocates NHP resources from routine screening to risk confirmation, providing an actionable roadmap for mechanism-based and welfare-conscious preclinical development.

records.title: AI-Enhanced CRISPR-Cas9 Therapeutics: Advances in Precision, Safety, and Delivery.
records.abstract: CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing has transformed biomedical research and is advancing toward clinical translation. The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) offers improved precision in guide RNA design, off-target prediction, and delivery optimization. This review synthesizes recent advances in CRISPR-Cas9 for medical applications, covering core mechanisms, engineered variants, base and prime editors, and therapeutic applications including CAR T-cell and CAR-NK engineering, genetic disorders, infectious diseases, and regenerative medicine. Delivery strategies are evaluated with emphasis on AI-driven optimization. AI applications are highlighted across deep learning architectures for guide RNA design, AI-designed nucleases such as OpenCRISPR-1, structure-guided and AI-assisted design of compact high-fidelity SaCas9 variants, reinforcement learning for pipeline optimization, and roles in CAR T-cell therapy and safety assessment. Safety challenges are examined, including off-target effects, chromosomal rearrangements, immunogenicity, and regulatory concerns. Future directions emphasize multi-scale modeling, explainable AI, clinical validation, and integration with synthetic biology, single-cell sequencing, organoids, and nanomaterials. The convergence of AI and CRISPR-Cas9 holds substantial potential for personalized medicine.

records.title: Optimized feeder-dependent culture enables efficient hypothalamic-pituitary organoid induction from human pluripotent stem cells.
records.abstract: Human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC)-derived hypothalamus-pituitary organoids recapitulate key processes of pituitary development in vitro, where cellular interactions between hypothalamic and oral ectodermal lineages are essential for organoid formation. However, how maintenance culture conditions for hPSCs influence the processes of lineage specification remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate that feeder-dependent culture conditions critically determine lineage specification during organoid formation. hPSCs maintained on SNL feeders preferentially differentiated into oral ectodermal cells, whereas maintenance on MEF feeders favored hypothalamic lineages. Co-culturing SNL- and MEF-maintained hPSCs or combining their conditioned media effectively balanced these lineages, enhancing pituitary induction efficiency. Furthermore, a stabilized FGF2 mutant enabled a "weekend-free" protocol that reduced labor and cost while maintaining high differentiation efficiency. Our findings underscore the significance of maintenance conditions and hypothalamus-oral ectoderm interactions in pituitary development, establishing a robust platform for efficient and reproducible generation of hypothalamus-pituitary organoids.

records.title: Artificial Cells and Biomimetic Cells: Intelligent Systems Driving a Paradigm Shift in Drug Discovery and Delivery.
records.abstract: The convergence of synthetic biology, materials science, and artificial intelligence drives a transformative shift in biopharmaceutical research, advancing from passive drug carriers to intelligent, programmable therapeutics. This review evaluates artificial and biomimetic cells as a framework that connects fundamental biological discovery with clinical translation. It examines five key technological pathways: membrane-engineered artificial cells, membraneless organelle (MLO) systems, multicompartmental artificial cells, protocell communication networks, and virtual cells. These platforms enable precise regulation of drug stability, targeting, biosynthesis, and adaptive responsiveness. Recent progress includes microenvironment-triggered release, logic-gated intercellular communication, and virtual cell-assisted high-throughput screening and toxicity prediction. Despite these advances, challenges remain in scalable manufacturing, long-term stability, and regulatory adaptation. The integration of closed-loop learning, interpretable models, and advanced biomanufacturing will be essential to position artificial and biomimetic cell systems at the forefront of next-generation precision medicine.

records.title: The Tenocyte from Atom to Cell: A Critical Multiscale Synthesis Linking Collagen Chemistry, Tissue Mechanics, Cell Mechanobiology and Mathematical Modelling.
records.abstract: The tenocyte builds, maintains, senses and degrades one of the most mechanically demanding extracellular matrices in vertebrates, yet the chemical, physical, biological and mathematical descriptions of this system have developed in largely separate literatures. This review examines the tenocyte-matrix unit as a single causal system spanning eight orders of magnitude in length, organised around five transitions: from collagen chemistry to molecular mechanics; from molecule to fibril and fascicle; from tissue loading to the cellular mechanical stimulus; from stimulus to transcription; and from cellular output back to matrix composition. At each transition, we weigh competing hypotheses, identify where evidence is decisive and where it remains correlative, and state the governing equations. We integrate advances from 2021-2026, including single-cell and spatial transcriptomic atlases of human tendons, the establishment of PIEZO1 as a causal regulator of tendon stiffness, and microstructurally derived constitutive models. We argue that tendon homeostasis is a closed-loop control problem, formalised as a mechanostat with an inverted-U dose-response, and that the recurrent pathologies of tendon-tendinopathy, ageing, diabetic stiffening and fibrotic healing are failures of this loop rather than of any single component. An open-source computational companion (tenocyte-virtual-cell) is introduced, and a prioritised research agenda closes the review.

records.title: Primary-Tumor Transcriptomic Signatures Associated with Circulating Tumor Cells Status in Breast Cancer: From CTC-Negative Remodeling to CTC-Associated Metastatic Programs.
records.abstract: Background/Objectives: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) play a central role in metastasis by enabling tumor dissemination through the bloodstream. However, the molecular transition from CTC-negative (CTC-) to CTC-positive (CTC+) states and their associated systemic remodeling remain poorly understood. Methods: We performed a transcriptomic comparison between CTC+, CTC-, and healthy individuals using RNA-seq data and a bioinformatics pipeline. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were subjected to functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, survival modeling, and drug perturbation prediction to delineate the molecular determinants of CTC emergence and persistence. Results: Primary tumors from CTC+ patients exhibited distinct transcriptomic profiles characterized by the upregulation of genes involved in PI3K-Akt signaling, extracellular matrix organization, and chromatin regulation (e.g., HDAC1, JUN, KLK10), alongside the downregulation of immune activation pathways, including complement, B-cell receptor (BCR), and T-cell receptor (TCR) signaling. Multi-gene survival models derived from upregulated (KLK10, MEOX2, IRS4, RND2) and downregulated (ALDH3A1, PPP2R2B, IGF1R) hub genes significantly stratified patient outcomes (HR = 1.74-2.44, p < 0.01). In contrast, primary tumors from CTC- patients displayed early systemic transcriptional alterations relative to healthy controls, with 1700+ DEGs linked to MAPK/ERK and receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) signaling pathways, suggesting pre-metastatic immune reprogramming even before CTC detection. Drug repurposing analysis identified Trichostatin A, BX-795, and Alvocidib as candidate compounds capable of reversing the CTC+ transcriptional signature. Conclusions: Rather than supporting a strictly binary view of CTC status, our findings are consistent with a transcriptional continuum of distinct yet partially overlapping primary-tumor transcriptional states associated with CTC- and CTC+ status, highlighting a molecular shift from immune suppression to epigenetic adaptation that facilitates hematogenous dissemination. The identified multi-gene prognostic panels and small-molecule candidates provide a foundation for CTC-targeted therapeutic strategies and early detection biomarkers in breast cancer.

records.title: Single-Cell Whole-Transcriptome Detection Expands the Observable RNA Space for AI Virtual-Cell Models.
records.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing has supplied cell atlases and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled virtual-cell models with scalable, gene-level descriptions of cellular state. Yet prevalent poly(A)-based counting assays capture only part of the RNA landscape. Here, "single-cell whole-transcriptome detection" denotes sequencing-based efforts to detect a broader range of RNA biotypes than conventional poly(A)-based gene counting; no assay detects or quantifies every cellular RNA species without bias. We compare RNA-capture scope, transcript-structure resolution, temporal labeling, spatial context, and additional modalities as distinct measurement dimensions. From a biosensing perspective, analytical sensitivity, transcript coverage, throughput, and assay bias determine which signals are available to computational models. We then examine cell-state representations, regulatory networks, dynamics, perturbation prediction, and foundation models. Total-RNA assays reveal additional non-coding RNAs, long-read methods inform transcript structure, and temporal assays constrain RNA kinetics. Whether these signals improve prediction beyond conventional gene-count inputs requires matched, task-specific model comparisons. We distinguish molecular observability, statistical association, predictive performance, and causal validation, which requires appropriate interventions. We propose benchmarks controlling sequencing depth, cost, model architecture, and held-out samples while testing feature ablations, out-of-distribution performance, uncertainty calibration, and experimental outcomes. Together, high-throughput poly(A)-based profiling and broader RNA measurements provide complementary cellular breadth and regulatory depth.

records.title: Virtual cells: progress and challenges from mechanistic modeling to data-driven integration.
records.abstract: Virtual cells aim to represent cellular states computationally and predict responses to genetic, chemical, environmental, temporal, and spatial conditions. For comparative purposes, this review uses state encoding (E), state transition (T), and observation decoding (D) as a conceptual abstraction spanning explicit mechanistic models, data-driven foundation and perturbation models, multimodal systems, and spatial and multiscale simulation. We examine model boundaries, data foundations, resource disclosure, out-of-distribution evaluation, causal evidence, and experimental validation. Independent benchmarks show that parameter count and training-set size do not automatically yield robust out-of-distribution generalization, while transcriptomic representations alone do not capture the full functional state of a cell. Trustworthy virtual cells will require perturbation-responsive transitions, cross-modal alignment, continuous-time dynamics, mechanistic constraints, calibrated uncertainty, independent experimental validation, and, where appropriate, closed-loop experimental feedback.

records.title: Progress of metabolomics-centric multi-omics research in medicine.
records.abstract: Metabolomics reveals molecular changes at the metabolic level during biological processes. Recent advancements, particularly through integration with other omics and artificial intelligence (AI), are advancing metabolic data analysis and multi-omics interpretation. This review introduces a "metabolomics-centric" paradigm as a conceptual framework for multi-omics integration, positioning metabolic readouts as the functional anchor for interpreting genotype-phenotype relationships. It also chronicles the evolution and medical applications of integration technologies. Our discussion first traces the field's evolution from bulk to single-cell and spatial methodologies, next surveys integration strategies to uncover mechanistic insights, and finally examines how AI-driven multimodal data integration and AI-optimized metabolomics workflows tackle persistent biological and computational challenges. Looking forward, this review identifies the AI virtual cell as a pivotal future direction for metabolomics-based multi-omics integration, calling for increased attention to its development to simulate dynamic molecular phenotypic networks within a multi-omics context.

records.title: An educational activity tailored for undergraduate students on AI-driven nanobody design for targeted antiviral therapeutics.
records.abstract: Protein-based biologics are converging at an unprecedented pace as generative artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes early-stage drug discovery. Nanobodies, single-domain antibody fragments derived from camelid heavy chain-only immunoglobulins, are an emerging class of antiviral biologics prized for their small size, stability, and access to cryptic viral epitopes. Traditional nanobody discovery relies on animal immunization and phage display screening, a process that can take 6 to 12 months and is entirely inaccessible within a standard undergraduate laboratory session. Here, we describe a succinct, in silico-based laboratory activity that uses a generative AI protein design server, GeoFlow-V3 (https://prot.design/), to allow undergraduate students to design a novel antiviral nanobody against the influenza A virus (IAV) hemagglutinin (HA) protein. This activity builds on our group's prior use of generative AI for undergraduate siRNA design teaching and extends the same pedagogical model to structural protein engineering. To our knowledge, this is the first use of a generative AI protein design platform for teaching nanobody design at the undergraduate level.

records.title: Protein nanocages: Programmable biomaterial platforms for therapeutics, bioimaging, and diagnostics.
records.abstract: Protein nanocages are monodisperse, hollow structures formed through the symmetric self-assembly of protein subunits. Their genetically encoded architectures combine the geometric precision of nanoscale assemblies with the intrinsic biocompatibility and functional versatility of naturally evolved proteins. Well-defined internal cavities and engineerable interior and exterior surfaces enable the spatial organization of therapeutic cargoes, molecular recognition elements, and bioactive components within a single nanoscale platform. In this Review, we examine the structural organization, self-assembly mechanisms, physicochemical properties, and functional diversity of representative protein nanocages, including ferritin, the pyruvate dehydrogenase E2 core, DNA-binding proteins from starved cells (Dps), small heat shock proteins (sHSPs), encapsulins, and lumazine synthase. We discuss how their structural features and assembly behavior govern biological performance and support biomedical applications in targeted drug delivery, cancer immunotherapy, vaccine development, and in vivo and in vitro diagnostics. Beyond describing individual platforms, we establish a unifying framework that positions protein nanocages as programmable molecular organizers and highlights five transferable design principles: multivalent ligand display, spatial compartmentalization, receptor-guided targeting, reporter organization and signal enhancement, and stimulus-responsive cargo release and functional activation. We also examine persistent challenges in structural stability, immunogenicity, scalable manufacturing, and clinical translation, alongside emerging opportunities in protein engineering, synthetic biology, and computational protein design. Collectively, these principles establish protein nanocages as versatile biomaterial platforms for integrating sensing, targeting, imaging, and therapy within a single molecular architecture, providing a foundation for next-generation precision nanomedicine. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Reviews typically treat protein nanocages individually, obscuring shared structural features and the extent to which design strategies transfer across systems. This Review addresses this gap by establishing a comparative framework spanning structurally diverse nanocages and distilling their similarities into a concise set of generalizable design principles. It reframes protein nanocages not merely as passive delivery vehicles but as programmable molecular scaffolds that organize cargo with controlled spatial arrangement and stoichiometry. This framework provides biomaterials researchers with a transferable basis for engineering protein assemblies for precision nanomedicine while identifying key challenges in structural stability, immunogenicity, and scalable manufacturing that must be addressed to facilitate clinical translation.

records.title: Bone morphogenetic protein 4 meets artificial intelligence: a comprehensive review of AI-driven advances in drug discovery, structural modeling, and clinical translation.
records.abstract: Bone Morphogenetic Protein 4 (BMP4), a member of the transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) superfamily, plays pivotal roles in embryonic development, tissue homeostasis, and disease pathogenesis-including cancer, fibrosis, and fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP). The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methodologies over the past 5 years has created unprecedented opportunities for understanding and therapeutically targeting BMP4 biology at multiple scales, from atomic-resolution structure prediction to population-level clinical prognostication. This review systematically examines the intersection of BMP4 biology and AI across three core domains: (1) AI-driven drug discovery targeting BMP4 signaling pathways, (2) deep learning-based protein structure prediction and computational modeling of BMP4 and its receptor complexes, and (3) clinical AI applications for BMP4-associated diseases. A narrative review with systematic search elements was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, bioRxiv, and arXiv for English-language publications from 2020 to 2026, supplemented by targeted searches via Semantic Scholar. Included studies were categorized as BMP4-specific, BMP receptor/BMP-pathway-targeted, or transferable AI methodology not yet applied to BMP4. We find that AI has accelerated BMP4-related research along multiple axes, though with important caveats. AlphaFold3 and related tools have generated high-confidence predicted models of BMP4-receptor complex architecture, aspects of which were previously intractable to experimental structure determination; these predictions remain to be fully validated experimentally. ML-guided virtual screening has identified first-in-class BMP pathway (receptor) modulators for FOP, although BMP4-specific small-molecule modulators have not yet been identified computationally. Single-cell transcriptomics combined with machine learning have revealed BMP4's context-dependent roles in glioblastoma cell state transitions and cancer-associated fibroblast biology; and LASSO-Cox regression models incorporating BMP4 expression have shown promising prognostic value in pancreatic adenocarcinoma and gastric cancer, pending prospective validation. Significant gaps persist-most notably the absence of BMP4-specific de novo protein design efforts, the scarcity of large-scale training datasets for BMP4-targeted drug discovery, and the limited integration of multimodal AI approaches in BMP4 clinical research. The convergence of BMP4 biology and AI represents a fertile research Frontier. While foundational tools are now in place, realizing the full translational potential of AI-augmented BMP4 research will require coordinated efforts in data generation, model development, and rigorous experimental and clinical validation. We outline priority directions for the next 5 years (approximately 2026-2031).

records.title: LM2KM: feature extraction from pretrained protein and molecular language models combined with quantum mechanics (QM) features for K M predictions.
records.abstract: The Michaelis constant (K M) is a key parameter for characterizing enzyme-substrate interactions and plays an essential role in enzyme kinetics modeling and physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) applications. However, experimental determination of K M is labor-intensive, and existing computational prediction approaches remain limited in accuracy and scalability. In this study, we systematically evaluated pretrained protein and molecule language models for K M prediction by integrating four protein language models (PLMs) and two molecule language models (MLMs) to encode enzyme sequences and substrate structures, respectively. Principal component analysis (PCA) was applied to reduce feature dimensionality, and a wide range of representation combinations were assessed. Our results indicated that protein representations derived from the last four layers of ProtT5 using approximately 70 features, combined with 20 CLS-based molecular features from MolFormer, provided a well-balanced and efficient representation for K M prediction. In addition, the incorporation of quantum mechanics (QM) descriptors consistently improved prediction performance across all tested configurations, with the model R 2 of 0.537. In summary, this work provides a flexible and extensible framework for large-scale K M prediction, with strong potential to facilitate enzyme pathway identification, drug and lead screening, and sequence-based protein design, supporting broader applications in enzyme kinetics-driven modeling and drug development.

records.title: Physics-Based AI-Augmented Workflows Discovering Candidate Graphene Quantum Dot Near-Infrared Chromophores.
records.abstract: Graphene quantum dots (GQDs) exhibit optical properties that depend strongly on their size, edge structure, and surface functionalization, but identifying the molecular structures responsible for near-infrared (NIR) emission remains challenging because of their structural complexity and disorder. In this work, we developed a computational framework combining rule-based molecular generation, semi-empirical quantum chemistry calculations, machine learning, and time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) to predict possible chemically realistic candidate GQDs with NIR-emitting optical properties. A fusion-based hexagonal lattice growth approach was used to generate 100,000 candidate graphitic structures. A random subset of 5000 structures was selected for semiempirical calculations. Computed band gaps were used to train and evaluate five machine learning models (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, and Neural Network). LightGBM predicted bandgaps were used to pre-screen the remaining 95,000 structures. 11,000 structures with low predicted gaps were selected for semiempirical calculations, and 50 top candidates with low gap and low SA score were selected for TD-DFT calculations employing LC-ωPBE functional. All 50 structures were predicted to exhibit NIR emission, offering a computed database of candidate NIR-emitting GQDs for future validation against experiment.

records.title: AI-guided De Novo design of DHPS inhibitors.
records.abstract: Hypusine modification of eIF5A by Deoxyhypusine Synthase (DHPS) is essential for the replication of a broad range of viruses, making DHPS an attractive host-directed therapy (HDT) target for antiviral drug discovery. AI-based drug design methods spanning binding affinity prediction and de novo molecular generation are rapidly proliferating, yet systematic benchmarking of diverse algorithmic paradigms under identical conditions on a shared target, with experimental validation, remains scarce. Here, we present an integrated AI benchmarking pipeline targeting DHPS and evaluate the full process from computational prediction to experimental validation. We compared 13 MM-GBSA score estimation models and 10 de novo molecular generation methods under 5-seed repeated experiments. For the prediction task, we propose an Out-of-Fold stacking ensemble integrating gradient boosting, graph neural networks, and chemical language models, achieving the highest Spearman rank correlation of 0.861 among all compared models. For the generation task, we propose RL-Design, a reinforcement learning-based framework using the ensemble predictor as a scoring oracle. RL-Design achieved the highest hit rate of 92.02% and maintained drug-like physicochemical properties across generated molecules, outperforming all nine competing methods. Moreover, experimental dose-response assays confirmed inhibitory activity in all three predicted-active compounds, with two highly active compounds showing IC50 values of 31.2 and 49.1 µM. Predicted and experimental activity showed complete concordance across all six tested compounds, providing oracle-independent validation of the pipeline. This pipeline provides a reproducible framework for AI-guided, target-specific inhibitor design and demonstrates the feasibility of HDT-focused antiviral drug discovery through systematic AI benchmarking.Scientific contributionThis work proposes two methods for inhibitor discovery against DHPS, a host-directed antiviral target. A predictive model for MM-GBSA binding-score estimation and a generative model that designs candidate hit compounds both ranked first among previous prediction and generation models under identical benchmarking. The predicted activities were experimentally confirmed by dose-response enzymatic assays.

records.title: Quantitative and mutational properties in the ctDNA uncovered by systemic inflammation in large B-cell lymphoma.
records.abstract: Risk assessment of large B-cell lymphomas (LBCLs) using liquid biopsy (LB) has so far focused primarily on the genomic properties of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), overlooking the host response. We previously identified an inflamed serum protein signature that reflects systemic host response and correlates with survival. Here, we integrated the inflammation signature and ctDNA to connect inflammation to genomic alterations and defined how this crosstalk informs treatment outcomes in two independent LBCL cohorts from Nordic phase II trials. We identify initiation of immune evasion at multiple genomic levels in patients with an inflammatory serum profile and uncover distinct mutational signatures that reflect diagnostic subtypes and inflammatory host response. We describe the added prognostic value of multimodal LB assessment, where patients with high levels of both ctDNA and inflammatory serum proteins have the worst overall survival (hazard ratio 7.93, p < 0.001) and progression free survival (hazard ratio 5.35, p < 0.001), thereby improving the risk estimate compared to either of the markers alone. This advanced multimodal LB employs clinically critical information on lymphoma and the host, both of which are essential for accurate treatment decision-making.

records.title: Nanomaterial-Enabled Electrochemical Biosensing Platforms for Circulating Tumor Cell Analysis.
records.abstract: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) are valuable liquid biopsy markers for assessing tumor heterogeneity, monitoring minimal residual disease (MRD), and guiding personalized therapy. However, their rarity in blood and phenotypic changes during epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) limit reliable detection. Electrochemical interfacial biosensors offer a promising solution due to their high sensitivity, miniaturization potential, and compatibility with microfluidics. This review summarizes recent advances in nanomaterial-enabled electrochemical CTC biosensing, focusing on interface engineering, signal transduction, and clinical translation. We highlight strategies such as multivalent recognition, engineered nanotopography, antifouling interfaces, and stimulus-responsive release that enhance CTC capture in whole blood. We also discuss nanozyme-based amplification, ratiometric calibration, and multiplexed electrochemical detection for phenotypic profiling beyond simple enumeration. Finally, we outline key translational requirements, including standardized benchmarking, clinical cohort validation, and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted data analysis. Integrating nanostructured interfaces with multiplexed detection and standardized whole-blood validation may accelerate electrochemical CTC analysis toward routine, phenotype-aware liquid biopsy.

records.title: Beyond blood: a narrative review of advancements in saliva-based diagnostics.
records.abstract: Human whole saliva is an accessible, noninvasive biofluid reflecting systemic and oral physiology, offering a viable alternative to invasive venipuncture and its associated pre-analytical vulnerabilities (e.g. ex vivo glycolysis). This narrative review synthesizes salivary biomarkers across major clinical domains, focusing on glycemic control (glucose, 1,5-anhydroglucitol, α2-macroglobulin), cardiovascular risk indices (cTnI, hs-CRP, sAA), critical care and sepsis surveillance (IL-10, acute-phase proteins), endocrinology (free steroid hormones), infectious diseases (HIV, HCV, SARS-CoV-2), oncological liquid biopsy (exosomal miRNAs, ctDNA), and neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer's disease (Aβ42, p-tau181, lactoferrin). Analytical modalities - ranging from high-sensitivity immunoassays to wearable electrochemical biosensors and mass spectrometry - are critically evaluated. Furthermore, this review delineates regulatory-cleared diagnostic platforms (FDA PMA/510(k), EUA, CE-IVD, and SAMHSA-certified panels for viral antibodies, late-night salivary cortisol, and toxicology) from emerging discovery-phase panels. Widespread clinical translation remains constrained by unstandardized collection protocols, oral matrix interference, and a lack of normative reference intervals. Transitioning salivary testing into mainstream diagnostics requires three priorities: (1) universal sampling standardization incorporating flow-rate normalization, (2) engineering matrix-matched biosensors tailored for sub-picomolar detection, and (3) rigorous multicenter prospective trials to validate definitive clinical cutoffs, dynamic blood-saliva correlation kinetics, and digital point-of-care integration.

records.title: Urine sediment (uSed) in molecular diagnosis of genitourinary cancer: From materials to methods.
records.abstract: Urine sediment (uSed) has often been treated as a residual pellet of urinalysis. Here, we reframe it as a biosource for molecular diagnosis in genitourinary (GU) cancer, yet its promise lies less in the molecules it contains than in the methods that make them interpretable. uSed carries tumor-derived DNA, RNA, proteins, and metabolites that capture genetic, epigenetic, transcriptional, proteomic, and metabolic alterations, enabling early detection, risk stratification, therapeutic monitoring, and minimal residual disease surveillance. Its molecular cargo determines biological reach, whereas analytical methods determine the reliability of clinical readouts. This Materials-to-Methods distinction is essential because the field remains rich in discovery but poor in validation: high diagnostic accuracy is frequently reported, yet few uSed assays are prospective, externally validated, or shown to change clinical management. We therefore synthesize uSed as a distinct urine fraction, separate from whole urine, cell-free supernatant, and extracellular vesicles, and evaluate how pre-analytical variability, analytical rigor, and post-analytical evidence grading determine whether molecular signals become clinically actionable. We propose that uSed research must shift from marker discovery to method-defined clinical utility, integrating standardization, external validation, and multi-omic/artificial intelligence approaches within a single translational framework. In this view, uSed is a complementary biosource for molecular diagnosis, not a substitute for tissue biopsy or established clinical pathways.

records.title: Circulating and extracellular vesicle-associated non-coding RNAs in diabetic retinopathy: a stage-aware framework for network-informed biomarker panels.
records.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a progressive microvascular complication of diabetes in which prognosis and management change substantially across non-proliferative and proliferative stages. Current imaging accurately detects established structural and vascular abnormalities but provides limited insight into early molecular changes or the risk of clinically important transitions within non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR). Circulating non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), and circular RNAs (circRNAs), have emerged as candidate biomarkers because they regulate pathways involved in endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, oxidative stress, and angiogenesis and can be detected in blood and extracellular vesicle (EV)-associated fractions. In this structured narrative review, we synthesize circulating and EV-associated ncRNA evidence within a stage-aware framework aligned with three clinical use cases: early screening, risk stratification within NPDR, and monitoring at the severe NPDR-early proliferative diabetic retinopathy boundary. miRNAs currently provide the most mature evidence for stage-associated expression patterns and, in selected studies, stage-discriminatory performance. By contrast, circulating lncRNA and circRNA evidence remains limited and is predominantly cross-sectional and advanced-stage associated, supporting their use mainly as complementary, network-informing components. EV association may improve RNA stability and enrich disease-relevant signals, but it does not establish retinal origin, and differences in biofluid source, EV isolation and characterization, normalization, and systemic confounders limit cross-study comparability. Importantly, direct evidence for clinically relevant adjacent-stage discrimination and longitudinal prediction remains scarce. We therefore propose that future biomarker development should prioritize stage-aware, network-informed multi-ncRNA panels, standardized pre-analytical and EV workflows, adjustment for major clinical confounders, and longitudinal imaging-integrated validation to determine whether these biomarkers add value beyond conventional retinal staging.

records.title: Clinical stewardship for medical AI translation: A systematic review of technological, human, and organizational barriers.
records.abstract: Medical artificial intelligence (AI) systems may perform well in controlled evaluations, yet challenges remain in their translation and implementation into routine clinical practice. This systematic review examines 247 original studies identified through searches limited to 2024-2025 publication dates and 31 clinical and translational journal titles. The most frequently coded translation-relevant evidence indicator is retrospective design (158 studies, 64.0%), followed by demographic or geographic data limitations (125, 50.6%), lack of qualifying independent external validation (71, 28.7%), small sample or data scarcity (51, 20.6%), and noisy or context-dependent labels (33, 13.4%). Categories are not mutually exclusive, and the estimates describe the sample defined by these filters, rather than all medical AI research. We integrate these findings with a "clinical stewardship" framework that distributes responsibility across clinical teams, developers, health systems, and patients while preserving the capacity of AI to reduce routine workload.
